title: rotini contract document
description: The contract document `rotini generate` writes when the conf sets generate.contract.file: every visible command of a cli with its inputs, output and exit statuses. Each command maps directly onto a tool definition for an AI agent: `name` and `summary` describe it, `parameters` is the JSON Schema of its arguments and flags, and `output` the JSON Schema of its result. Every embedded schema is standard JSON Schema (draft-07), and a `$ref` in one resolves against this document's `definitions`.

format.description: The document's format and its version. A change that would break a reader changes the number.

commands.description: Every visible command, the root first and then depth-first in spec order. A hidden command, and everything beneath it, is left out. A plugin a command declares follows it, with `plugin: true`.

definitions.description: The spec's named schemas, as JSON Schema, by name.

errors.description: The JSON Schema of one line rotini.StructuredReporter writes to stderr: an error, warning, info or success. A program uses that reporter only when its author opts in.

completion.description: What the program's shell completion lets its users switch. Present only when the cli declares something here.

messages_env.description: The environment variable that hides completion messages when set to 0, false or off.

descriptions_env.description: The environment variable that hides the descriptions shown beside completion candidates when set to 0, false or off.

response_files.description: How the program reads response files: before the first `--`, a word starting with the prefix is replaced by the named file's lines, one argument per line. A caller passing an argument that starts with the prefix writes it after `--`, or doubles the prefix (`@@x` is the argument `@x`). Present only when the cli reads response files.

prefix.description: The character that starts a response-file word, such as @.

name.description: The command as typed, the root included: "taskr list".

path.description: The command names below the root: ["list"]. Empty for the root.

deprecated.description: Why the command is deprecated, when it is.

plugin.description: true for a plugin: a separate program the command runs, whose inputs and output this document does not describe.

options_first.description: true when flags must come before the command's first argument: every word after that argument is an argument, flag-shaped words and `--` included.

flags.description: The command's own flags, then the cascading flags it inherits from its ancestors.

parameters.description: An object schema with one property per argument and flag, by name, each carrying its summary as `description`: the input schema of a tool definition.

output.description: The shape of what the command writes to stdout when it succeeds, when it declares one. A command that writes a stream of items declares one item.

variadic.description: true when it takes every remaining positional. When arguments follow it, they take the last positionals and it takes the ones in between.

passthrough.description: true when raw words start at this argument: it and every word after it are taken as typed, flag-shaped words and `--` included. A word starting with - that should be its first word is written after `--`.

cascading.description: true when the command declares it and every command beneath it accepts it too.

inherited.description: true when an ancestor declares it as cascading.

short_circuit.description: true when setting it on the command line waives the command's required inputs and other rules, as --help does: an agent can pass it without supplying anything else.

env.description: The environment variables the flag falls back to when it is not on the command line, in lookup order: the first one set wins.

config_key.description: The config file key the flag falls back to after its environment variables. Present only when the command reads config files.

repeatable.description: false when giving the flag more than once on the command line is an error rather than the last value winning. Absent means repeats are accepted.

variables.description: The environment variables read, the first preferred.

secret.description: true when the value is a secret; its default is then left out.

key.description: The key read from the configuration file.

file.description: The name of the configuration file it is read from, when one is named.

required.description: true when an empty stdin is an error.

output.description: What the command still writes to stdout when it exits with this code.

EnumValues.description: What each of the input's enum values declares beyond its spelling, by value. Present only when some value has a summary. The schema's own `enum` lists the values only.

summary.description: One line saying what the value means.
